You can also switch to Programmer mode for hex/binary calculations or Graphing mode for visualizing math functions.

instruction: How do I permanently delete files in Windows so they can't be recovered?
output: To prevent recovery, use the cipher command: open Command Prompt and type cipher /w:<folderpath> (e.g., cipher /w:C:\SecureDelete) to overwrite free space in that area. For drives, use format with the full format option (not quick format) which overwrites all sectors. Third-party tools like Eraser provide scheduled secure deletion with multiple overwrite passes. For SSDs, a full format or using the manufacturer's secure erase tool is most effective.

instruction: How do I export a PowerPoint presentation as a PDF?
output: In PowerPoint, go to File > Export > Create PDF/XPS Document. Click 'Create PDF/XPS'. Choose a save location and filename. In the options, you can choose to include or exclude notes, set the publish range (all slides, current slide, or a range), and choose PDF quality. Click 'Publish'. The presentation will be saved as a PDF that preserves the layout and can be viewed without PowerPoint installed.

instruction: How do I password-protect a file in Windows?
output: Windows doesn't have a built-in file password feature, but you can use several methods: (1) Use 7-Zip (free) — right-click a file, select 7-Zip > Add to archive, set a password with encryption. (2) In Microsoft Office apps (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), go to File > Info > Protect Document > Encrypt with Password. (3) Use BitLocker to encrypt an entire drive. For sensitive files, encryption is much more secure than simple password protection.

instruction: How do I install a font in Windows?
output: Download the font file (.ttf or .otf format) from a trusted source. Right-click the font file and select 'Install' to install it for your user account, or 'Install for all users' to make it available to everyone on the computer. The font will then appear in the font lists of applications like Word, PowerPoint, and Photoshop. You may need to restart the application for the new font to appear.

instruction: How do I enable clipboard history in Windows?
output: Press Windows + V to open the clipboard history panel. If it's your first time, Windows will prompt you to turn on the feature — click 'Turn on'. Once enabled, pressing Windows + V shows your recent clipboard items and you can click any to paste it. Go to Settings > System > Clipboard to manage clipboard history settings. You can also pin frequently used clipboard items so they're always available.

instruction: How do I set up a new Wi-Fi network connection in Windows?
output: Click the Wi-Fi icon in the system tray. A list of available networks appears. Click the network you want to connect to. Click 'Connect'. If it's a secured network, type the Wi-Fi password when prompted and press Enter or click 'Next'. Check 'Connect automatically' if you want Windows to connect to this network automatically whenever it's in range. The network will be saved in your connection history.

instruction: How do I configure screen timeout in Windows?
output: Go to Settings > System > Power & sleep. Under the 'Screen' section, set the timeout duration for when the screen turns off — separately for 'On battery power' and 'When plugged in'. You can choose from preset options or select 'Never' to disable automatic screen timeout. Shorter timeouts save power on laptops. If you want the computer to also sleep after a period, adjust the 'Sleep' settings below.

instruction: How do I use Windows Spotlight as my lock screen?
output: Go to Settings > Personalization > Lock screen. Under 'Personalize your lock screen', select 'Windows Spotlight' from the dropdown menu. Windows Spotlight automatically rotates through beautiful images from Bing, often with interesting facts about the locations shown. The images update regularly and you can give feedback on them (like/don't like) using the icons on the lock screen to refine what types of images are shown.

instruction: How do I configure a static IP address in Windows?
output: Go to Settings > Network & Internet. Click your connection type (Wi-Fi or Ethernet) and select your network > Properties (or click 'Change adapter options', right-click your adapter > Properties). Select 'Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4)' and click Properties. Choose 'Use the following IP address' and enter your static IP, subnet mask, and default gateway. Enter your DNS servers (e.g., 8.8.8.8 for Google) and click OK. Confirm the address doesn't conflict with other devices.

instruction: How do I remove an email account from Outlook?
output: In Outlook, go to File > Account Settings > Account Settings. In the Email tab, select the account you want to remove and click 'Remove'. Confirm the removal when prompted. Note that removing the account from Outlook does not delete the actual email account — it just disconnects it from Outlook. If you're removing a Microsoft account that's also used for Windows sign-in, there may be additional steps.

instruction: How do I use PowerPoint's Presenter View during a slideshow?
output: When presenting with a second screen or projector, go to the Slide Show tab and check 'Use Presenter View'. When you start the slideshow, Presenter View appears on your screen while the audience sees only the slides. Presenter View shows the current slide, next slide preview, speaker notes, elapsed time, and slide navigation tools. If Presenter View appears on the wrong screen, click 'Display Settings' within Presenter View to swap displays.

instruction: How do I reduce the size of a PowerPoint file?
output: Large PowerPoint files are usually caused by high-resolution images. To reduce size: go to File > Compress Media to compress embedded videos and audio. For images, click an image and go to Picture Format > Compress Pictures — choose 'Web (150 ppi)' or lower resolution and check 'Delete cropped areas of pictures'. Also go to File > Save As and choose a new file to strip any autosave versions. Removing unused slide layouts also helps.

instruction: How do I add slide numbers to a PowerPoint presentation?
output: Go to Insert > Slide Number. This opens the Header and Footer dialog. Check 'Slide number' to add numbers. Optionally check 'Don't show on title slide' to skip the first slide. Click 'Apply to All'. If the slide number doesn't appear, the slide layout may not include a number placeholder — you can add one by going to the View tab > Slide Master and editing the master layout to include the slide number placeholder.

instruction: How do I record a PowerPoint presentation with narration?
output: Go to the Slide Show tab and click 'Record Slide Show'. Choose to start from the beginning or current slide. The recording interface will open. Use the Record button to start narrating each slide. Advance slides normally while narrating. The recording saves audio (and optionally video from your webcam) for each slide. When done, click Stop. The timings and narration are saved with the presentation and will play back when you run the slideshow.

instruction: How do I undo changes in PowerPoint?
output: Press Ctrl+Z to undo your most recent action in PowerPoint. Press it multiple times to undo several actions in sequence. To redo an action you've undone, press Ctrl+Y. You can also click the undo and redo arrow icons in the Quick Access Toolbar at the very top of the PowerPoint window. PowerPoint maintains an undo history for the current session — closing the file clears the undo history.

instruction: How do I align objects on a PowerPoint slide?
output: Select the objects you want to align (hold Shift and click each one). Go to the Home tab or Picture Format/Shape Format tab and click 'Arrange' > 'Align'. Choose an alignment option: Align Left, Center, Right (horizontal), or Align Top, Middle, Bottom (vertical). Select 'Distribute Horizontally' or 'Distribute Vertically' to space multiple objects evenly. You can also turn on alignment guides via View > Guides for visual snapping assistance.

instruction: How do I convert a PowerPoint presentation to a video?
output: Go to File > Export > Create a Video. Choose the video quality (Full HD 1080p, HD 720p, etc.). Decide whether to use recorded timings and narrations or set a default time per slide. Click 'Create Video', choose a save location, and select the file format (MP4 recommended). PowerPoint will render the presentation to a video file. This is useful for sharing presentations with people who don't have PowerPoint installed.

instruction: How do I change the slide size in PowerPoint?
output: Go to the Design tab and click 'Slide Size'. Choose 'Standard (4:3)' or 'Widescreen (16:9)', or click 'Custom Slide Size' to enter specific dimensions. PowerPoint will ask whether to Maximize or Ensure Fit when resizing — 'Ensure Fit' scales content down to fit the new size (safer), while 'Maximize' may crop content. Widescreen is the modern standard for presentations on most displays and projectors.

instruction: How do I add a hyperlink to a PowerPoint slide?
output: Select the text or object you want to add a link to. Go to Insert > Link (or press Ctrl+K). In the Insert Hyperlink dialog, choose 'Existing File or Web Page' for external links and type or paste the URL. Choose 'Place in This Document' to link to another slide. Choose 'E-mail Address' for mail links. Click OK. During the presentation, clicking the linked text or object will navigate to the linked destination.
